metadata.title: Supra Interact | The Ultimate Smart Contract Interactor
metadata.description: Professional smart contract interactor, testing environment, and interaction suite built specifically for the Supra ecosystem. Connect your wallet, explore modules, and execute transactions seamlessly on Testnet and Mainnet.
metadata.keywords: Supra, Blockchain, Smart Contracts, Explorer, DApp, SupraOracles, Move Language, Web3, Hoglet DAO

Governance.factoryNotPublished: The governance factory is not published yet. Set NEXT_PUBLIC_GOVERNANCE_FACTORY to your deployed module address.
Governance.connectWallet: Connect a wallet to audit your own address
Governance.statusHint: Read from the blockchain itself, not from what the contract claims about itself.
Governance.statusUnmanaged: Untouched — the master key still works and nobody else has been given control
Governance.statusRenounced: Given up — nobody can ever act for it again
Governance.statusDaoGoverned: Managed — the address has no key of its own and the admin is in charge
Governance.statusHazard: Warning: the master key still works, so the admin can be ignored
Governance.factImmutable: Nothing can ever change it again
Governance.factCryptoFrozen: Every way to act has been destroyed
Governance.factAdminIsContract: A contract governs it, not a plain account
Governance.emptyHint: Paste any address to find out who really controls it: whether its master key still works, who is in charge, and whether anything can ever change it again.
Governance.hazardDetail: The master key behind this address still works, so whoever holds it can ignore the admin: act on its own, or take the control back. Do not call this decentralized until the key is destroyed.
Governance.burnBody: This is the step that makes everything above permanent. It overwrites the master key of this address with zeros. After this, nobody can ever act for it again — not you, not anyone.
Governance.burnAssetWarning: Every coin, fungible asset and NFT still sitting in this address becomes permanently unspendable. Sweep the account before continuing.
Governance.burnGateSwept: I have moved every asset out of this address.
Governance.burnGateUnderstood: I understand the master key will be destroyed forever and cannot be recovered.
Governance.burnDoneHint: The key is now all zeros. Refresh the state to see where this address landed: given up for good, or governed by an admin with no way back.
Governance.burnFailed: Could not submit the key rotation
Governance.stage_dual_master: Stage 2 · you and the admin can both act
Governance.stage_governed: Stage 3 · only the admin can act
Governance.runnerConnectWallet: Connect a wallet to run the lifecycle on your own address.
Governance.runnerUnmanagedBody: Nothing is deployed under this address yet. Create a module with no key at all and give it an owner.
Governance.runnerDualMasterBody: The master key still works, so it can still override the admin. Destroy it below to make this permanent.
Governance.runnerDualMasterContractsBody: The master key still works, so it can still override the owner. That is an account-level hazard: destroying the key lives in Account Control, not here.
Governance.runnerGovernedBody: The key is gone and the admin is in charge. Upgrades, handovers and the final freeze are available.
Governance.runnerFrozenBody: Nothing can ever change this again. There is no key, no control and no way back for anyone.
Governance.deployFormHint: Creates a new account with no key at all, and hands control to an admin address.
Governance.fieldDaoAdminHint: The address that will own this contract. It is the admin on-chain, and the only one that can upgrade the code, renounce it permanently, or hand it on. Putting a multisig, timelock or DAO here is what makes it decentralised — your own wallet works too, but then you keep the control and no collective ever gets a say.
Governance.fieldNewAdminHint: Hand ownership to any address — a multisig, a timelock, a DAO, or another account.
Governance.transferFormHint: One atomic step. There is no two-step confirmation, so a typo here is unrecoverable.
Governance.govContractHint: Only this contract is affected. Every package is its own resource account with its own admin, so a hand-over or renounce here never touches the others.
Governance.transferFormConfirmLabel: New owner — type it again to confirm
Governance.transferFormWarning: If the new admin is wrong or unreachable, nobody can ever govern this module again.
Governance.upgradeTargetMismatch: This package is compiled for {target}, not the account being upgraded ({contract}). Rename the package so it derives that account.
Governance.deepFreezeFormHint: Publishes the final version of the code on {address}, then destroys every way to act for it.
Governance.deepFreezeFormWarning: The version you upload here becomes permanent. After this the module can never be upgraded again.
Governance.deepFreezeFormAck: I understand this bytecode is final and can never be replaced.
Governance.sealToggleHint: Publish this version and freeze the contract forever. Nothing - not you, not a later version of the factory - can ever change it again.
Governance.renounceFormHint: Destroys every way to act for {address}, for good.
Governance.renounceFormWarning: Every way to act is destroyed and the handover is undone. Nobody can reverse this — not even a later version of the factory.
Governance.renounceFormConfirmLabel: This contract — type its address to confirm
Governance.donateFormTitle: Hand this account to an admin
Governance.donateFormHint: One transaction. The factory itself calls the framework's public `offer_signer_capability` for you — all it needs from you is the delegation proof that only your private key can produce.
Governance.donateSignHint: Reads the sequence number this transaction will consume and signs the signed-message payload the framework verifies.
Governance.donateSubmitHint: Registers the delegation with the vault so the admin you chose can govern this address.
Governance.donateProofNote: Signature only. No gas, no transaction. Submit sends the single donation transaction that carries it.
Governance.burnFrameworkOnly: The factory cannot do this for you. `rotate_authentication_key_call` is declared `entry` (not `public`) in the framework, so Move forbids calling it from any other module — only the key owner can send it directly. Every other step in this lifecycle is orchestrated by the contract, because the functions it needs are public.
Governance.burnOwnerOnly: Only the owner can burn this key, so connect the wallet for this address to continue.
Governance.selfRenounceTitle: Or give up this account for good
Governance.selfRenounceBody: Destroy the key with no admin involved. The account is given up for good: nothing can ever change it again, nobody can act for it, and there is no vault record. Note that this closes the delegation route — once the key is gone you can no longer hand it to an admin.
Governance.cancelDelegationBody: Takes the handover back: it recovers the control you gave away and forgets the account, so this one can be handed to an admin again later. Use it if you chose the wrong admin or handed it over from the wrong wallet.
Governance.cancelDelegationWindow: Only possible while your key still works. That is exactly the risk the key destroy removes — once the key is gone the handover is final and only the admin can give up control.
Governance.cancelDelegationOwnerOnly: Only the owner of this key can cancel its delegation, so connect the wallet for this address to continue.
Governance.cancelDelegationDoneHint: The control is back in your hands, and this account can be handed to an admin again whenever you want.
Governance.burnGatesHint: Tick both acknowledgements above to continue.
Governance.burnReauditHint: Re-reads the chain so the new stage shows. Nothing is sent.
Governance.termEoa: EOA — an account controlled by a single private key. It is simply the account your wallet signs for.
Governance.termAdmin: The on-chain role that owns a contract: the only address that can upgrade its code, renounce it for good, or hand it on. The screens here call it the contract owner.
Governance.termRenounce: Renounce — give up control permanently, so nobody (not even you) can ever act for that address again.
Governance.termCapability: Capability — the stored right to act for an account. It is an object, not a password, and it can be destroyed forever.
Governance.termImmutable: Immutable — the code can never be changed or upgraded again, by anyone.
Governance.glossaryTitle: What do these protocol words mean?
Governance.donateNeedAdmin: Fill in the contract owner above first - the signature is worth nothing without it.
Governance.donateProofValid: Signature valid for the current address. It survives edits to the field above; only a new transaction can invalidate it.
Governance.donateOneDelegate: One account, one delegation. If this account already answers to an admin, handing it to a different one would take the control away from them — cancel the current delegation first.
Governance.burnBlockedTitle: Do not destroy the key yet
Governance.burnBlockedBody: This account was handed to an admin, but its delegation no longer points at this vault's proxy — someone else holds it now. If you destroy the key you can never take it back: undoing a delegation needs the key you would be destroying.
Governance.burnBlockedHint: Put your admin back in charge first, or move the account to an admin you control. Burning the key here does not restore anything — it only makes the loss permanent.
Governance.hubContractsSubtitle: A module with no private key, published to its own resource account. Hand control to any address, or renounce it for good.
Governance.hubAccountsSubtitle: Hand this account to an admin, take the control back, or destroy the key so nobody ever can.
Governance.runnerAccountUnmanagedBody: Nobody is in charge of this account yet. Hand it to an admin, or destroy the key so it can never be used again.
Governance.runnerAccountGovernedBody: The key is gone and an admin is in charge of this account. Nothing else can be done here: changing what this account hosts is contract governance, not account control.
Governance.otherSurfaceBody: This account was handed to an admin. The actions for that state belong to Account Control, which is a separate tool on purpose.
Governance.govRenounceReveal: I understand this cannot be undone — reveal
Governance.myContractsSubtitle: Modules this wallet deployed through the vault. Pick one to upgrade it, transfer its admin, or renounce it for good.
Governance.interactorGovernanceError: The factory did not answer. It may be unreachable, or not published at the configured address.
Governance.interactorGovernanceUnknown: This factory has no record of this address.
Governance.interactorGovernanceUnknownHint: That is not a clean bill of health. It means control cannot be established from here — the address may still be governed by a key, a multisig, or a capability held elsewhere.
Governance.interactorGovernanceFrozenHint: Every signer and capability for this address was destroyed. Nobody can change it again, including a later version of the factory.
Governance.interactorGovernanceGovernedHint: The factory holds the capability, so a registered admin can still upgrade it, hand it over, or renounce it.
Governance.keyUpgradeableHint: This contract has an active authentication key, meaning the deployer can still upgrade these modules or sign transactions.
Governance.keyResourceAccountHint: This account has no private key of its own (AuthKey is 0x0). It may be permanently renounced, OR it may be a Resource Account controlled by a SignerCapability stored elsewhere, such as a multisig.
Governance.keyAdminRotatedHint: This contract's authentication key was rotated to another address. Upgrades are controlled by that external admin or multisig.
Governance.myContractsEmpty: This wallet has not deployed any contract through the factory yet.
Governance.myContractsPick: Select a contract on the left to manage it.
Governance.contractAuditHint: Paste the module's address. You will sign with the wallet that is its admin — they are usually two different accounts.
Governance.flowDonateTitle: How handing over your account works
Governance.flowDonateStep1: You sign once. A copy of your signer capability is delegated to a brand new empty account — no code, no modules, nothing but the right to act for you.
Governance.flowDonateStep2: The vault can now act for your account: upgrade what it hosts, freeze it, or give it up for good — and only the admin you chose can ask for that.
Governance.flowDonateStep3: Your key still works, so the whole thing is reversible: you can take that ability back at any time while the key is alive.
Governance.flowDeployStep1: Your code is published to an account derived from your address, so it lands in the same place every time and you can know that address before you build.
Governance.flowDeployStep2: The owner you choose takes over from the start. It is the only address allowed to upgrade, freeze or hand the module on.
Governance.flowDeployStep3: Nothing is final yet. You can upgrade it, move it to a different admin, or seal it for good — the module keeps its own admin the whole time.
Governance.flowDonateWarning: The factory can act for this account — and you can take that ability back, but only while your key is alive. Destroying the key is what makes it final: the factory keeps nothing of yours, because the key was never given to it, only a copy.
Governance.flowDeployWarning: This account has no key of its own, so the owner is the only way in. Choose it carefully — and you can still change it later, or seal the module so it can never change again.
Governance.workspaceSeedHint: Optional. Empty uses the package name; otherwise it must be a valid package name (letters, digits, _). Use it to reproduce the address a contract was deployed under.
Governance.workspaceNeedAddress: Connect your wallet to resolve the target address for this package.
Governance.workspaceBadPath: A module path must look like sources/Name.move
Governance.workspaceNeedOne: A package needs at least one module
Governance.workspaceNote: Saves in this browser and resumes on the same account. Compiling is free and publishes nothing; the deploy step is what writes on-chain.
Governance.deployManualFiles: Compiling here returns module ids, not the bytecode the publish needs. Upload the build output to deploy.
Governance.workspaceTomlBrokenHint: The package name and its named address must both be declared in this manifest, and the address must be the account this package publishes to ({address}). Anything else compiles cleanly and then fails on-chain after you have signed. You can keep editing other parts, such as adding a dependency.
Governance.workspaceTomlWarnHint: The service requires a pinned rev for every dependency and checks the organisation itself. These notes are about reproducibility; anything it rejects comes back with its own reason.
Governance.workspaceBadName: Use a name like Pool, or a full path like sources/Pool.move
Governance.workspaceCodeSizeHint: Comment-stripped source size - a live estimate of the package before it is compiled. The service's limit is {max}.
Governance.workspaceAdvancedHint: Leave these on default for a normal compile. Included artifacts (none is the smallest) trims what the on-chain package metadata carries, for a large package. Override size check lets the service hand over artifacts past its size cap.
Governance.workspaceNoneNotShown: none publishes without the source map: the contract works, but it will not be shown on the explorer.
Governance.workspaceChunkUnavailable: Chunked publishing is not available on Supra, so a package this large has to shrink (included_artifacts: none) or be split into smaller packages.
Governance.workspaceSaveQuota: This browser's storage for this site is full. Export the project to keep your work.
Governance.workspaceSaveBlocked: This browser is blocking storage (private mode or blocked cookies). Export the project to keep your work.
Governance.workspaceFrameworkNoise: {count} note(s) from the framework sources — not your files, and safe to ignore.
Governance.workspaceCopyAiPromptHint: Copies a prompt for an AI assistant carrying this package's layout, its framework pin, and the exact address it must be published to.
Governance.workspaceImportFailed: Could not read that selection as a Move package.
Governance.workspaceImportEmpty: That selection had no .move or .toml files. Pick the package folder, or select its sources directly.
Governance.workspaceImportSkipped: {count} file(s) were skipped: they did not fit the package layout.
Governance.deployNeedAdmin: Enter the contract owner address above.
Governance.deployImmutableToggle: Make it immutable from the start
Governance.deployImmutableHint: Publishes the package and freezes it in the same transaction - no owner is kept.
Governance.deployImmutableWarning: No owner will be set. This contract is frozen the moment it is published: nobody, not even you, can upgrade or renounce it later.
Governance.deployNeedMetadata: The package metadata is missing. Upload package-metadata.bcs from your build output.
Governance.deployNeedBytecode: The module bytecode is missing. Compiling above returns module IDs, not the bytes the publish needs — upload the .mv files from bytecode_modules/.
Governance.workspaceArtifactsOmitted: The package compiled, but its artifacts exceed the service's 8 MB limit and were not returned. Export the project and build it locally to deploy.
Governance.workspaceArtifactsHint: Each module's compiled bytecode - the exact payload publish sends on-chain. Expand a module to review its hex or copy it.
Governance.workspaceDeployTargetHint: The account this package will be published to. It is derived from your address and the package name, so each name gets its own account.
Governance.workspaceTemplateBasicHint: Two functions and one import: enough to call something and read the result.
Governance.workspaceTemplateFullHint: Adds the chain clock and an entry that emits an event, so you can send a transaction and not only a read.
Governance.deployTargetTaken: This package name already has a contract at {address}. Publishing will update it, not create a second one — you must be its admin.
